verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol spec explicitly documents an HTTP 402 flow: when a merchant server returns 402, the agent presents a signed 'payment IOU' as part of the Agentic Payment Container, and the merchant can grant access before settlement — this matches the no-checkout-UI, pay-per-call machine payment pattern the story describes. However, this is one line within a broader agentic-checkout spec rather than a dedicated API-monetization product; there's no documented developer flow, SDK, or pricing guide framed around 'monetize your API/service with 402' the way dedicated x402-style tools are marketed. Missing for 10: a dedicated API-monetization guide/SDK, concrete pricing/settlement mechanics for per-call billing, and independent/hands-on confirmation that developers have used this specifically to gate API access.
